original_benchmark.notes: AMA-Bench open-end QA: 208 episodes, each with one long agent trajectory and 12 memory QA pairs (types A=Recall, B=Causal, C=State Update, D=Abstraction). Primary metric is LLM-as-judge accuracy (Qwen3-32B at temperature 0). Harbor additionally logs token-level F1 per QA for inspection; it is not part of the reward.

harbor_adapter.notes: alfworld-10 subset: 10 alfworld episodes (EMBODIED_AI, ids 30-39), 120 QAs per run. One Harbor task is one AMA-Bench episode; the agent answers all 12 QA pairs in a single Answer[1]..Answer[12] block written to /workspace/answers.txt, and the reward is the mean LLM-judge score across the 12 QAs. Parity runs the same Claude Code agent on both sides over the same raw trajectory.jsonl (ama-bench_parity_claude_code_alfworld.yaml on Harbor 0.27.0; --method claude_code upstream at commit d2d5715), graded by claude-haiku-4-5 on both sides, 3 runs per side. See parity_experiment.json.

random-30 subset: stratified random sample of 5 episodes per domain across the 6 domains (seed 42), 360 QAs per run. One Harbor task is one AMA-Bench episode; the agent answers all 12 QA pairs in a single Answer[1]..Answer[12] block written to /workspace/answers.txt, and the reward is the mean LLM-judge score across the 12 QAs. Parity runs the same Claude Code agent on both sides over the same raw trajectory.jsonl (ama-bench_parity_claude_code_random.yaml on Harbor 0.27.0; --method claude_code upstream at commit d2d5715), graded by claude-haiku-4-5 on both sides, 3 runs per side. See parity_experiment.json.
